principles.title: Design System Principles
principles.subtitle: AtomDesignToken eliminates temporary procedural hardcoding, combining platform-agnostic Single Source of Truth (SSOT), browser-native standards, and a 4-tier AI Lego Assembly Pipeline to build enterprise-grade UI.

ssot.title: Single Source of Truth (SSOT)
ssot.subtitle: All design decisions derive from a single unified data specification.
ssot.description: When Figma, Markdown guidelines, or token JSON files serve as the benchmark, the entire codebase must auto-generate. Developers are strictly prohibited from hardcoding raw HEX values or magic numbers inside components.
dos: All colors, spacing, and radiuses must reference var(--atom-*) semantic tokens.
When a new style is required, define it inside the token specification (tokens.json) first.
donts: Do not inline raw values like #3182F6 or 16px into component CSS or Tailwind classes.
Do not duplicate independent theme variables across different pages.

zero-runtime.title: Zero Runtime Overhead
zero-runtime.subtitle: Minimize browser runtime calculations and leverage native platform capabilities.
zero-runtime.description: Prevents CSS-in-JS runtime parsing costs and JS bundle bloat. Pre-compiled with native CSS Custom Properties (--*) and static classes for instant 0ms style injection.
dos: Utilize CSS standard variables to achieve instant theme switching at the browser engine level.
Bundle into static CSS files to maximize First Contentful Paint (FCP) performance.
donts: Do not depend on heavy runtime style injection libraries that parse style objects on every render.
Avoid global state subscriptions that trigger full component tree re-renders upon theme changes.

three-tier.title: 3-Tier Token Hierarchy
three-tier.subtitle: Global Palette -> Semantic Intention -> Component Scoped Tokens
three-tier.description: Always maintain an intentional semantic tier between raw palette values and components. This layer enables multi-brand, dark mode, and high-contrast switches without touching component code.
dos: Prioritize Tier 2 (Semantic: --atom-bg-surface, --atom-color-primary) for all UI styling.
In dark themes, switch Tier 2 reference mappings rather than mutating Tier 1 base palettes.
donts: Never reference Tier 1 raw values (var(--blue-500)) directly in component code.
Avoid using Tier 3 component tokens inside generic layout containers.

framework-agnostic.title: Framework-Agnostic Design
framework-agnostic.subtitle: Operates identically across React, Vue, Svelte, Angular, and pure Vanilla HTML.
framework-agnostic.description: A design system must never be coupled to a specific JS framework. Built on open web and CSS standards to maintain 100% visual consistency across polyglot stacks.
dos: Author layouts against standard CSS custom variables and semantic HTML5 elements.
Enable legacy HTML or jQuery environments to achieve identical styling purely via class names.
donts: Never create non-standard dependencies that break styling without specific framework runtimes.

predictable-naming.title: Predictable Naming Convention
predictable-naming.subtitle: Strictly structured hierarchy: [Namespace]-[Category]-[Concept]-[Variant]-[State].
predictable-naming.description: Tokens must clearly communicate their purpose and scope to both developers and designers at a glance, adhering to W3C DTCG token naming recommendations.
dos: Use standardized descriptive names (e.g., --atom-color-primary-hover, --atom-space-4).
Prioritize explicit semantic meaning over cryptic abbreviations.
donts: Do not declare ambiguous or context-free names (e.g., --atom-color-1, --atom-size-box).

accessibility.title: Accessibility by Default (A11y)
accessibility.subtitle: All semantic color pairings satisfy WCAG 2.1 AA 4.5:1 contrast ratios.
accessibility.description: Accessibility is an intrinsic foundation validated at token generation, not an afterthought. Standard pairings guarantee immediate contrast and legibility.
dos: Validate 4.5:1 (normal text) and 3:1 (large text) contrast ratios across text/surface token pairings.
Supplement color cues with accessible visual indicators (icons, underlines, luminance contrast).
donts: Never strip focus rings or outline accessibility cues (outline: none).
Do not use low-contrast muted gray tokens for essential body copy.

anti-pattern-prevention.title: Anti-Pattern Prevention & Polish
anti-pattern-prevention.subtitle: Eliminate AI Slop and unnecessary noise in favor of Swiss minimalist restraint.
anti-pattern-prevention.description: Defends against LLM visual clichés like garish neon gradients, thick side borders, and excessive bounce animations in accordance with Impeccable standards.
dos: Use subtle 1px borders, status dots, and soft tints instead of heavy unilateral borders.
Apply natural deceleration curves (ease-out, 200-300ms) with micro-fades instead of cartoonish bounces.
Run `npm run lint:design` (impeccable detect) before commits for zero-token static validation.
donts: Avoid side-tab tells such as thick left borders (border-l-4) on cards or sidebars.
Do not inline gratuitous purple gradients or heavy drop shadows.
Avoid wrapping every element in floating cards regardless of visual hierarchy.

ai-governance-pipeline.title: AI Governance: 4-Tier Assembly Pipeline
ai-governance-pipeline.subtitle: Tokens ➔ Components ➔ Blocks ➔ UX Patterns (Component-First Assembly)
ai-governance-pipeline.description: All AI coding assistants (Cursor, Claude Code, Antigravity, Copilot) must follow the verified 4-tier assembly pipeline. When a new UI element is required, create atomic components in components/ui/ first before assembling higher-order blocks.
dos: Define pure atomic components in components/ui/ first, then import them to build blocks.
Strictly use semantic CSS variables (var(--atom-*), var(--text-primary)) for all styles.
Provide complete empty, loading/skeleton, error, and keyboard accessible states.
donts: Never bypass the component tier by writing inline raw tags (<button>, <div class="rounded-lg...">) directly in blocks or pages.
Never hardcode raw Tailwind color utilities (text-blue-500, bg-gray-100).

ai-roles-skills.title: 4 AI Specialized Roles & Agent Skills
ai-roles-skills.subtitle: Collaborative task force: token-guardian, component-architect, block-designer, docs-curator
ai-roles-skills.description: AtomSystem delegates responsibilities across 4 roles to prevent LLM hallucinations: token-guardian (token integrity), component-architect (atomic UI), block-designer (content blocks & patterns), and docs-curator (E2E & docs). `npx atomsystem init` installs the skill automatically.
dos: Instruct your AI using "Follow the Component-First rule" or "Respect atom.design.md tokens".
Verify code modifications with official `npm run lint:design` (impeccable detect).
Let the AI convert design guide markdowns into DTCG tokens.json via the atomsystem skill.
donts: Never allow the AI to generate monolithic single-file components exceeding 500 lines.
Never inline domain datasets directly inside view-layer components.

tokens.description: Defines all UI design decisions—colors, fonts, spaces, and radiuses—as platform-agnostic atomic data. Fully compliant with the W3C DTCG standard as zero-runtime CSS variables.

componentsDoc.relatedPatternsTitle: Production UX Patterns Using This Component

layout-spacing.name: Layout & Spacing Specs
layout-spacing.description: Standard 8-point spacing scale, Container constraints, Stack distributions, and Grid responsive layouts.
useCases: Standardizing padding and margin scales across all UI components (4px to 64px)
Ensuring visual consistency across horizontal and vertical element gaps using Stack
Responsive container max-width constraints and column gutter alignment
usagePatterns: Use standard CSS variables (var(--atom-space-*)) instead of arbitrary pixel values.
Apply 8px increments for standard element flow and 24px+ for section separation.

dosAndDonts.do: Adopt 8-point multiples (8px, 16px, 24px, 32px) as the first choice.
dosAndDonts.dont: Do not use rogue utility values such as gap-[13px] or p-[7px].

color-status.name: Color & System Status
color-status.description: Brand identity colors, semantic status states (Success, Warning, Destructive, Info), and theme-reactive surface pairings.
useCases: Communicating core brand identity via Primary and Secondary CTA elements
Semantic status feedback mapping for Success (Green), Warning (Amber), and Destructive (Red)
Surface tokens (bg-primary, bg-secondary) enabling seamless light/dark mode transitions
usagePatterns: Reference semantic intent tokens (var(--atom-color-*), var(--atom-status-*)) over raw hex values.
Maintain at least 4.5:1 contrast ratios across text and surface pairings adhering to WCAG 2.1 AA.

dosAndDonts.do: Map destructive actions strictly to Destructive danger tokens.
dosAndDonts.dont: Do not sprinkle random neon red or arbitrary tailwind colors across standard interfaces.

typography.name: Font & Typography Scale
typography.description: Complete typography hierarchy scale ensuring legibility and Swiss modernist visual structure (Display, Heading, Body, Caption).
useCases: Prominent hero titles and promotional display text
Hierarchical document headings from H1 to H4
Body copy legibility with Body-1 (14px) and Body-2 (16px)
Metadata and timestamps using Caption (12px)
usagePatterns: Use composite tokens binding font size, line height, letter spacing, and weight together.
Standardize UI body copy on 14px (var(--atom-font-body-1)).

dosAndDonts.do: Structure typographic ladders hierarchically: Display > H1 > H2 > Body > Caption.
dosAndDonts.dont: Never use unreadable micro-fonts under 10px in mobile or compact views.

button.name: Button (Button Variants)
button.description: Production-ready button set combining 3-tier visual hierarchy (Primary, Secondary, Ghost/Icon) and semantic system states (Brand, Success, Warning, Destructive).
useCases: Single primary conversion action per screen - Primary CTA (Save, Checkout, Sign up in brand color)
Neutral secondary actions in dialog modals - Cancel, Back, Previous step with Secondary / Outline
High-density table toolbars & filter bars - Icon-Only & Ghost buttons to minimize visual noise
Irreversible or critical actions - Destructive buttons for Delete, Cancel Order, Close Account
usagePatterns: Place at most one Primary action per viewport to guide unambiguous user focus.
Always provide aria-label for Icon-Only buttons to ensure screen reader accessibility.
When displaying loading spinners, keep width fixed and disable pointer events to prevent layout shifts.

dosAndDonts.do: Structure visual hierarchy logically: Primary > Secondary > Ghost.
dosAndDonts.dont: Do not place multiple Primary brand buttons side-by-side, causing decision paralysis.

dosAndDonts.do: Use semantic status colors (Red, Orange, Green) mapped to user action consequences.
dosAndDonts.dont: Do not use random inline color hex codes like bg-[#ff0000] instead of system tokens.

input.name: Input Field (Input)
input.description: Single-line text input field bound to standard border, surface, focus ring, and validation error tokens.
useCases: User authentication flows (Email, password, verification code)
Search query inputs and autocomplete fields
Checkout and billing information entry forms
usagePatterns: Always connect explicit <label> with htmlFor and input id for keyboard/screen reader accessibility.
Display inline validation error messages with aria-invalid when input is invalid.

dosAndDonts.do: Provide clear visual focus ring tokens when user tabs into the input.
dosAndDonts.dont: Do not hide labels or replace them solely with placeholder text.

selection.name: Selection (Switch & Checkbox)
selection.description: Interactive selection controls for immediate state toggling (Switch) and multi-selection agreements (Checkbox).
useCases: Immediate configuration toggles (Push notifications, Dark mode, Biometric login)
Terms of Service and Privacy Policy agreement checkboxes
Batch multi-row selection in data tables
usagePatterns: Use Switch for immediate on/off toggles without requiring a separate save button.
Use Checkbox when selection is part of a form that requires submission.

dosAndDonts.do: Ensure accessible tap target of at least 44x44px for touch screens.
dosAndDonts.dont: Do not use Switch when the action requires an explicit confirmation or submit click.

dialog.name: Modal Dialog (Dialog)
dialog.description: Modal window overlay requiring explicit user confirmation or presenting focused sub-workflows.
useCases: Financial transfer confirmations, final checkout steps, destructive delete confirmations
Focused single-task input wizards
usagePatterns: Trap keyboard focus inside the modal and allow dismissal with the Escape key.

dosAndDonts.do: Provide clear primary and secondary action buttons with distinct visual weights.
dosAndDonts.dont: Do not open multiple stacked modals simultaneously, disorienting users.

sheet.name: Bottom Sheet (Sheet)
sheet.description: Mobile-first drawer panel sliding from the bottom for quick contextual details and actions.
useCases: Mobile detail inspection, bottom action sheet filters, payment method selector
usagePatterns: Support swipe-to-dismiss drag gestures and backdrop tap to close.

dosAndDonts.do: Use smooth slide-in transitions with standard easing tokens.
dosAndDonts.dont: Do not overflow bottom sheets beyond viewport height without internal scrolling.

alert.name: Alert Callout (Alert)
alert.description: Contextual notification banner communicating system status, tips, or warning alerts.
useCases: Form submission error summaries, system maintenance notices, promotional banners
usagePatterns: Use semantic status colors (danger, warning, success, info) aligned with message severity.

dosAndDonts.do: Pair status colors with meaningful icons for colorblind accessibility.
dosAndDonts.dont: Do not use flashing or overly intrusive alerts for routine information.

tabs.name: Segmented Tabs (Tabs)
tabs.description: Segmented navigation control switching between views within the same context.
useCases: Account settings categories, framework code snippet switchers, dashboard period filters
usagePatterns: Support keyboard left/right arrow navigation between tab items.

dosAndDonts.do: Keep tab labels concise (1-2 words) for clean responsive wrapping.
dosAndDonts.dont: Do not use tabs for cross-page navigation; use global links instead.

badge.name: Status Badge (Badge)
badge.description: Compact pill badge for categorization, numerical counts, and real-time status indicators.
useCases: Order status (Pending, Shipped, Delivered), subscription tiers, new feature tags
usagePatterns: Keep badge content short and strictly secondary to primary text.

dosAndDonts.do: Use subtle background tints with high-contrast text for optimal legibility.
dosAndDonts.dont: Do not clutter cards with excessive badges competing for visual attention.

card.name: Content Card (Card)
card.description: Structured surface container grouping related information with subtle borders and elevation tokens.
useCases: Dashboard metric cards, product listing grids, account balance overview
usagePatterns: Maintain consistent padding tokens (var(--atom-space-4)) across card grids.

dosAndDonts.do: Establish clear internal typography hierarchy from header to body.
dosAndDonts.dont: Do not nest cards within cards more than 2 levels deep.

table.name: Data Table (Table)
table.description: W3C token-bound data grid for displaying structured records with hover and border states.
useCases: Transaction histories, member lists, administrative audit logs
usagePatterns: Align numerical and monetary columns to the right for easy scanning.

dosAndDonts.do: Provide responsive horizontal scroll containers for mobile viewports.
dosAndDonts.dont: Do not truncate essential data without providing a full tooltip or detail view.

layout.name: Layout & Stack (Layout & Stack)
layout.description: Page-level structure shells (Header, Sidebar, Content) and spacing token assembly tools (Stack, Grid).
useCases: Global enterprise dashboard shell (Top nav + Left sidebar + Main content)
Vertical stack alignment with standardized spacing tokens (gap="4")
Responsive card grid layouts (cols={3} gap="4")
usagePatterns: Compose layouts using Layout.Header, Layout.Sidebar, Stack, and Grid.

dosAndDonts.do: Use standardized gap tokens instead of arbitrary margin utilities.
dosAndDonts.dont: Do not use non-standard inline values like mb-[17px] or mt-[23px].

container.name: Responsive Container (Container)
container.description: Centered responsive container constraining max-width and applying automatic gutter padding.
useCases: Centered article reading views (size="md")
Standard web application main body (size="lg")
Enterprise data dashboard grids (size="xl")
usagePatterns: Choose container sizes matching page content density.

dosAndDonts.do: Use standard container size tokens (sm, md, lg, xl, 2xl).
dosAndDonts.dont: Do not hardcode arbitrary max-width styles like max-w-[1140px].

calendar.name: Calendar & DatePicker
calendar.description: Monthly calendar navigation, single and date range selection, today indicators, and disabled dates adhering to W3C accessibility standards.
useCases: Check-in and check-out date picking in reservation flows (hotels, flights, appointments)
Filtering financial and dashboard transactions by date periods (last 7 days, this month, custom ranges)
Date-of-birth and document expiration date input forms
Setting deadlines for task tracking and project milestones
usagePatterns: Visually distinguish between the selected date and "Today" so users quickly understand the current reference point.
Disable past or unavailable dates with reduced contrast to intuitively prevent invalid choices.
Provide a touch target of at least 36x36px for calendar date cells on mobile viewports.

dosAndDonts.do: Immediately reflect selected year/month/day in an input field or top header with clear formatting (YYYY-MM-DD).
dosAndDonts.dont: Do not wait until form submission to trigger error toasts for past dates; disable past date cells in the calendar.

dosAndDonts.do: Provide intuitive navigation arrows alongside year and month selector dropdowns.
dosAndDonts.dont: Do not force users to click previous month arrows 120 times when picking a birth date; provide decade or year jumpers.

select.name: Select & Dropdown
select.description: Custom dropdown picker with full keyboard navigation, fuzzy search filtering, and categorized group labels.
useCases: Country and region codes, currency (KRW/USD/EUR), and bank account selection
Product sorting options (Newest, Popular, Price: Low to High, Most Reviewed)
Admin dashboard date ranges and role-based access assignment
Quantity and shipping delivery memo dropdowns
usagePatterns: Use dropdown selects instead of radio buttons when there are 5 or more options to preserve screen real estate.
Include an inline search filter inside the dropdown when the list exceeds 15 items for rapid discovery.
Display the selected label and icon clearly on the trigger button after an option is chosen.

dosAndDonts.do: Provide a helpful placeholder like "Select an option..." when no value is selected.
dosAndDonts.dont: Do not bury only 2 or 3 choices inside a dropdown; segmented tabs or radio groups provide a much better experience.

accordion.name: Accordion & Collapse
accordion.description: Vertical expandable content panels for FAQs, terms of service, and dense configuration panels, reducing visual clutter.
useCases: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) and help center guides
Checkout step breakdowns (discount coupons, shipping address, payment methods)
Mobile settings and permissions toggles
Collapsible legal disclosures, terms of service, and privacy policies
usagePatterns: Place a rotating chevron icon on the right edge of each header to convey expansion state.
Ensure smooth height transitions to prevent jarring content shifts (CLS).

dosAndDonts.do: Formulate header titles as concise questions or key nouns so users can scan effectively.
dosAndDonts.dont: Do not leave every accordion panel open by default on page load, which creates unnecessary scroll fatigue.

tooltip.name: Tooltip & Popover
tooltip.description: Floating contextual overlay displaying supplementary tips when users hover or focus on icons or truncated content.
useCases: Viewing truncated text hidden behind ellipsis (...)
Helper explanations adjacent to complex financial terms (APR, DSR, amortization)
Describing icon-only buttons (Copy, Download, Settings, Refresh)
Explaining disabled button reasons on hover, such as "Insufficient permissions"
usagePatterns: Introduce a subtle 150-200ms delay to prevent accidental flashing when the mouse grazes the trigger.
Use collision detection to automatically flip tooltip placement when reaching viewport boundaries.

dosAndDonts.do: Keep tooltip text concise (1-2 sentences) and focused on supplementary context.
dosAndDonts.dont: Do not hide crucial action buttons or forms inside fleeting hover-only tooltips.

toast.name: Toast Notifications
toast.description: Non-blocking floating feedback notifications for success, warning, error, and background task updates.
useCases: Confirmation upon copying links or tokens to clipboard ("Copied to clipboard")
Save, delete, or update feedback messages in background workflows
Network reconnect or background sync failure warnings
Undo action confirmations ("Item moved to trash. Undo")
usagePatterns: Place toasts consistently at the top-right or bottom-center of the screen.
Auto-dismiss informational or success toasts after 3 to 5 seconds.
Keep persistent or explicit close buttons on destructive or critical error toasts.

dosAndDonts.do: Include an action button (e.g., "Undo", "Retry") when a reversible mistake occurs.
dosAndDonts.dont: Do not stack 10 consecutive toasts flooding the screen; cap simultaneous visible toasts to 3.

pagination.name: Pagination
pagination.description: Page-based navigation controls for browsing large data sets, supporting jump-to-page, prev/next, and ellipsis truncations.
useCases: Browsing product lists in e-commerce catalogs
Data tables with dozens or hundreds of ledger records
Forum discussion boards and search results
Audit log and transaction history feeds
usagePatterns: Clearly emphasize the currently active page with solid primary or accent styling.
Collapse large page ranges with ellipsis (...) while keeping first and last pages accessible.
Disable Prev on page 1 and Next on the final page.

dosAndDonts.do: Provide generous touch targets (at least 36x36px) for finger taps.
dosAndDonts.dont: Do not show pagination controls when the entire dataset fits on a single page.

radio.name: Radio Group
radio.description: Single-choice option selectors within mutually exclusive option lists, supporting keyboard arrow navigation.
useCases: Payment method selection (Credit Card, Bank Transfer, Apple Pay, PayPal)
Delivery speed options (Standard 3-5 days, Express Next-Day, Same-Day)
Language or locale switching in preferences
Single-answer quiz or survey questions
usagePatterns: Use radio groups instead of dropdowns when there are 2 to 4 options so all choices remain visible.
Support arrow key navigation (Up/Down or Left/Right) to switch active selections.

dosAndDonts.do: Ensure the accompanying text label is clickable together with the circular radio button.
dosAndDonts.dont: Do not use radio buttons for multiple selections; use checkboxes instead.

slider.name: Slider
slider.description: Continuous or discrete range selector for numeric inputs like price, volume, and percentage ratings.
useCases: Price range filters in e-commerce search results (e.g., $10 - $500)
Volume, brightness, and audio media player controls
Loan calculation sliders for term (months) and principal amounts
Font size and opacity adjustments in visual design editors
usagePatterns: Display the current numeric value in real-time above the thumb or in an adjacent badge.
Provide discrete tick steps for distinct increments (e.g., steps of 5 or 10).

dosAndDonts.do: Support keyboard arrow adjustments (Left/Right arrow) for accessible fine-tuning.
dosAndDonts.dont: Do not rely solely on tiny thumbs without direct text input fields when exact numbers matter.

avatar.name: Avatar & Profile
avatar.description: Circular or rounded visual identity component displaying user photos, initial letter fallbacks, and presence badges.
useCases: User profile icons in header navigation bars
Sender avatars in chat messenger and comment threads
Team member facepiles in collaborative document editors
Contact lists and assignees on Kanban project cards
usagePatterns: Render uppercase initials when no image URL is provided or when image loading fails.
Support status indicators (online green dot, busy red dot, offline grey ring) at the bottom-right corner.

dosAndDonts.do: Always provide descriptive aria-label or alt text with the person’s full name.
dosAndDonts.dont: Do not let broken image icon outlines appear when avatars fail to load; use smooth initial fallbacks.

progress.name: Progress Bar
progress.description: Deterministic and indeterminate progress indicators visualizing file uploads, multi-step forms, and system tasks.
useCases: File upload and asset downloading progress bars (0% to 100%)
Onboarding multi-step signup wizards (Step 2 of 4)
Storage quota utilization monitors (e.g., 42GB of 100GB used)
Crowdfunding goal completion meters
usagePatterns: Display percentage figures alongside progress bars to eliminate ambiguity.
Use indeterminate pulse or shimmer animations when exact duration cannot be calculated.

dosAndDonts.do: Include aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, and aria-valuemax for assistive screen readers.
dosAndDonts.dont: Do not use flashing neon colors; keep progress bar styling aligned with system semantic accents.

skeleton.name: Skeleton Loader
skeleton.description: Low-fidelity placeholder previewing content shapes while data loads, minimizing perceived latency and preventing layout shift.
useCases: Initial content placeholders for dashboard charts, cards, and profile headers
Feed and article card loading states in social platforms
Table row placeholders while API queries are in flight
E-commerce product grid loading placeholders
usagePatterns: Match skeleton geometry precisely to the anticipated final component dimensions.
Use a gentle shimmer gradient moving left-to-right rather than harsh flashing.

dosAndDonts.do: Set the width of paragraph text skeleton lines to roughly 60% on the final line to mimic real paragraphs.
dosAndDonts.dont: Do not make skeleton animations overly rapid or intense, which causes eye strain.

breadcrumb.name: Breadcrumb Navigation
breadcrumb.description: Hierarchical navigation trail illustrating the user’s current location within an Information Architecture (IA).
useCases: E-commerce category trees (Home > Women > Outerwear > Trench Coats)
Developer documentation structures (Docs > Components > Form > Calendar)
Admin dashboard directory and workspace browsing
Real estate listing locations (State > City > District)
usagePatterns: Use clean separators such as a slash (/) or right chevron (>) to guide reading direction.
Truncate deep middle path steps with ellipsis (...) or dropdowns on mobile viewports.

dosAndDonts.do: Treat the last item in the path as the active page; render it as non-clickable plain text.
dosAndDonts.dont: Do not overuse breadcrumbs on shallow single-depth screens.

separator.name: Separator & Divider
separator.description: Clean horizontal and vertical semantic dividers segmenting distinct content sections and UI action clusters.
useCases: Dividing account settings from destructive sign-out items in menus
Separator with "OR" label between social SSO and email password form inputs
Vertical bars (|) between header utility links
Demarcating card headers, content bodies, and footer buttons
usagePatterns: Use subtle border tokens rather than heavy black lines to preserve modern minimalist elegance.

dosAndDonts.do: Ensure appropriate vertical and horizontal margins based on orientation.
dosAndDonts.dont: Do not make dividers heavier or more prominent than actual content.

textarea.name: Textarea with Counter
textarea.description: Multi-line input field supporting live character counts, auto-resizing, and form validation states.
useCases: Customer support tickets and detailed feedback submissions
Community discussion posts and comment reply boxes
Delivery instruction notes and custom checkout requests
Multi-line AI prompt and markdown editors
usagePatterns: Display live character count feedback ("34 / 500") at the bottom-right when constraints apply.
Provide concise instructional placeholder text when the field is empty.

dosAndDonts.do: Reflect invalid error states with red border tokens and assistive error messages below the field.
dosAndDonts.dont: Do not configure min-height so small on mobile that only two words can be read at a time.

tree.name: Tree View
tree.description: Accessible hierarchical tree component representing nested directories, organization charts, and taxonomy branches.
useCases: IDE code file and folder workspace explorer trees
Organization charts, departments, and role-based access trees
Multi-level e-commerce catalog category trees
Documentation and knowledge base chapter indexes
usagePatterns: Provide clear expansion toggles (▶) on parent nodes with rotation animations upon opening.
Highlight selected items with gentle brand tints and semibold weight rather than clunky hard borders.
Draw subtle dashed vertical guide lines to clarify parent-child depth across deep trees.

dosAndDonts.do: Expand only 1 or 2 levels by default and allow users to drill down on demand.
dosAndDonts.dont: Do not expand thousands of deeply nested nodes at once, causing infinite vertical scrolling.

dosAndDonts.do: Support keyboard navigation with Space, Enter, and Arrow keys.
dosAndDonts.dont: Do not remove focus rings (outline: none) or rely solely on double-clicking.

layoutPage.title: Layout & Spacing System
layoutPage.description: Do not hardcode arbitrary pixel values (padding: 13px, gap: 27px) when building web screens. Build consistent rhythm and robust responsive layouts using AtomDesignToken's Container, Stack, Grid, and W3C DTCG spacing tokens.
layoutPage.containerDesc: Automatically controls optimal center-aligned width and responsive safety gutters to match screen width.
layoutPage.containerMaxWidthNotice: Max width: {width} (Horizontal gutter: auto 16px mobile, 24px desktop)
layoutPage.containerSm: Mobile forms, single login/signup cards, narrow dialogs
layoutPage.containerMd: Tablet body, blog posts, document reading views (readability optimized)
layoutPage.containerLg: Standard web apps, settings pages, profile management screens
layoutPage.containerXl: Standard desktop dashboards, 4-column card grids, data tables
layoutPage.container2Xl: Wide monitor monitoring consoles, financial chart feeds
layoutPage.spacingDesc: AtomDesignToken provides a 9-step spacing scale based on a 4px grid to eliminate random numbers.
layoutPage.space1: Inline icon & text gap, badge padding
layoutPage.space2: Button internal gap, compact list row gap
layoutPage.space3: Input field padding, small card internal padding
layoutPage.space4: Default mobile gutter, standard card padding, component base margin
layoutPage.space5: Medium card padding, modal section gap
layoutPage.space8: Document section margin, main layout gap
layoutPage.stackGridDesc: Easily compose layouts with token-based <Stack> and <Grid> without manually writing raw flex/grid CSS.
layoutPage.dosDontsTitle: Layout Design Rules & Anti-Pattern Prevention (Do's & Don'ts)
layoutPage.doItem1: Always adhere to var(--atom-space-*) or gap="4" token units for all spacing.
layoutPage.doItem2: Always wrap the top-level content of a page with <Container> to secure safe gutters.
layoutPage.doItem3: Assemble responsive card lists using <Grid cols={3}> without manual CSS media queries.
layoutPage.dontItem1: Do not write arbitrary magic numbers inline such as p-[13px] or margin-top: 27px.
layoutPage.dontItem2: Do not fix container width to width: 1200px to avoid causing horizontal scroll on mobile.
layoutPage.dontItem3: Do not break vertical rhythm by giving different margins to sibling elements inside a stack.
